notes: Five own pages read on dentrixascend.com (home, about, packages, Why Dentrix Ascend, and the own blog post cited by 3 answers), all HTTP 200 and not thin. C03 uses Henry Schein One's dentrix.com comparison page, read once in the Dentrix coding, because it is the vendor's own page covering both products. The 97 answers overlap heavily with the Dentrix bundle: statements whose subject is Dentrix or Henry Schein's lineup (two versions, Dentrix offers Ascend as its cloud path) are coded in the Dentrix file; statements whose subject is Ascend are coded here, including the separate-product statements (C04). The combined 35,000+ installations line is coded in the Dentrix file. tab32.com (cited by q6 Google AI Overviews 3) failed with a network error during cause tracing for C05 and is listed in needs_browser_read for that purpose only. Pass 2 (8 Oct 2026): the manifest has no browser read for any Dentrix Ascend page or for tab32.com, so no claim was re-classed and tab32.com stays in needs_browser_read. The gap lines and the comparison-table rows naming Ascend (Cloud, Cloud-Only, Cloud-Native, Custom, ~$399 to $1,200) all repeat claims already listed for the same answers, so no claim or instance was added. The consistency check kept C05 wrong: the about page states in so many words that Ascend is not a cloud-hosted version of on-premises software. Not coded: name-only mentions, Townie vote shares, ratings, capability descriptions (AI, multi-location dashboards), comparative cost remarks and the passing reference to an Ascend cloud quote in one ChatGPT table. Judgement call: C03 (cloud version of Dentrix) is classed true while C05 (cloud-hosted version of Dentrix) is wrong, because the about page denies only that Ascend is hosted on-premises software.
